_comment: UAE -> Italy waitlist registration. Inherits the shared flow from _default.json and overrides what this portal does differently.
_comment_vs_switzerland: Three real differences from AE-CHE, all of them structural rather than cosmetic: (1) the waitlist checkbox HAS a formcontrolname here, so it can be pinned properly; (2) 'Your Details' takes NO typed fields — you upload the passport bio page and VFS OCRs the details out of it; (3) there is an extra OTP step before review-pay, and that OTP goes to the registered MOBILE, not the email used at login.
_comment_enabled: OFF until the OTP step is implemented — see "otp" below. Everything up to it is configured and can be exercised with `doctor --route AE-ITA --walk`.
_comment_checkbox: Pinned, unlike Switzerland: this portal DOES bind the control, and a named control beats inferring one from position or wording. The label reads 'Currently No slots are available for selected category, please confirm waitlist'.

steps.name: your_details
steps._comment_no_typed_fields: This portal does NOT ask for name/passport/phone as typed inputs. It asks for the passport BIO PAGE, then extracts the data from it — the page even says 'the data extracted from it can't be edited'. So the whole applicant form is one upload field.
steps._comment_no_screenshots: This page RENDERS the uploaded passport, so a debug screenshot would write the photo, MRZ and signature to disk as pixels — which log redaction cannot reach. The evidence value of a screenshot does not justify keeping a copy of someone's passport on every run. Other steps still screenshot normally.
steps._comment_countdown: The page renders 'Please wait 8 seconds...' but it COUNTS DOWN — a capture partway through shows a smaller number than the real total, which is 30s, the same as Switzerland. Save enables before the timer expires yet does nothing until it does, so the wait is mandatory; 32s gives margin. Measured AFTER the upload and extraction, which are themselves several seconds in.

fields.name: passport_scan
fields._comment: The <input type=file> is hidden="" behind a styled 'Browse Files' button; set_input_files() targets the input directly, so the button is never clicked. Scoped to <app-file-upload> so it can never pick up some other file input on the page.
fields._comment_value: Path to the passport bio-page image or a ONE-PAGE PDF, from the client file. PNG/JPG/PDF only, max 2MB — VFS rejects anything else. An absolute path is safest; a relative one resolves against the working directory.
fields._comment_after_upload: The upload renders a preview with Continue / Replace. Continue commits the file and starts the extraction. NOTE this is a plain <button class='file-browse'>, NOT a mat-button — matched by its accessible name, which works for both.
fields._comment_wait_after: VFS OCRs the document server-side and fills the form from it. Nothing useful can be asserted until that finishes, and Save would be rejected with an empty form. 15s is a starting figure — raise it if a dry run shows Save still disabled.

steps.name: details_summary
steps._comment: Inherited from _default; restated only to document that this portal behaves the same way — the URL stays on /your-details and the content swaps to a summary.

steps.name: otp
steps._comment_position: POSITION MATTERS: this page sits between the details summary and /review-pay. Without "after" a new step is appended, which would put it AFTER the committing step and it would never be reached.
steps._comment_DISABLED: NOT IMPLEMENTED YET. This step needs a human-in-the-loop OTP relay: the code goes to the registered MOBILE, so it cannot be read from the login mailbox the way otp_flow.py reads the sign-in code. Planned as a Telegram round trip (bot asks -> you reply -> bot types it). Until that exists this step is disabled and the route is "enabled": false, so nothing can half-run into it.
steps._comment_page: Sits between the details summary and /review-pay. Shows a 'Generate OTP' button; clicking it sends the code and reveals an OTP input (type=password, maxlength=6) plus a Verify button, then Continue. 'Regenerate one-time password' is available, limited to 3 attempts before VFS logs the session off — so retries must be counted carefully.
steps._comment_shape: Recorded now so the implementation has a target to fill in:

steps.name: review_pay
steps._comment: Identical in shape to Switzerland's, including the duplicate-id problem: several boxes share 'mat-mdc-checkbox-1'. Matched by wording, not position.

fields.name: accept_terms
fields.label: I accept the
fields._comment: Terms and Conditions consent. Its <label> wraps an <a target='_blank'> to the T&Cs — clicking the label's centre opens that link instead of ticking, which is why fields.py targets the native input first.

fields.name: agree_waitlist
fields.label: Yes, I agree for waitlist confirmation
fields._comment: Unique wording, so no index — this keeps working if VFS reorders the consents. Note the on-page text ends with a full stop ('...confirmation.'); the match is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING, so omitting it is intentional and more robust.

confirmation._comment: UNVERIFIED for this portal — inherited from _default and not yet seen on a real Italy run. Switzerland showed 'Your Appointment is Waitlisted' at /confirmation; this one is left as the looser 'waitlisted' until a live run confirms the exact headline. Tighten it then.
